first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 6% and 4% respectively. memory_31 and memory_86 demonstrate that signup simplification and shortened onboarding directly improve these metrics. Verifying these two will confirm the magnitude and durability of those lifts before committing one experiment slot. memory_73 warns against promotional pricing in this competitive context—it damaged 30-day retention and would undermine long-term revenue sustainability. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) targets a different segment and doesn't address the self-serve activation decline. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers but won't solve new-customer activation problems. Activation messaging (memory_91) showed gains, but onboarding/signup friction is the root cause of current decline. Simplify onboarding at standard scale targets the core metrics degradation, aligns with proven playbook, and preserves long-term unit economics.

final.rationale: Verified source records confirm both signup simplification (+9% activation, +4% qualified revenue, minimal retention risk) and shortened onboarding (+13% completion, +3% retention lift, -2.1 days to value). Current metrics show activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—these declines map directly to the problems these interventions solved. Simplified onboarding is the highest-confidence lever available: it addresses both root metrics simultaneously, carries positive retention signal (exp_86 +3%), and proven sustainable. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is disqualified—it materially reduced 30-day retention and contradicts primary objective. Referral incentives and activation messaging are secondary tactics; onboarding friction is the primary blocker. Enterprise sales assist is orthogonal to self-serve SMB decline. Standard experiment scale allows measurement while preserving ability to expand if successful.
